messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name]

Date of Admission: [Date]

Date of Discharge: [Date]
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our hospital with persistent fever and diarrhea. The patient had a positive nasopharyngeal swab for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) RNA on real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Chest X-ray and chest computed tomography (CT) on admission demonstrated diffuse ground-glass opacity located predominantly at the periphery of the lower lung lobes.

The patient developed respiratory failure and renal failure due to COVID-19 and was intubated on a ventilator. The patient received methylprednisolone and was administered tazobactam− piperacillin and levofloxacin to rule out bacterial pneumonia. The patient was injected with unfractionated heparin to prevent thrombus formation.

The patient was extubated on day 4 after intubation as his respiratory condition improved. The steroid was then changed to oral prednisolone, which was given every second day at reducing doses. The patient had an increase in serum creatinine levels and was given temporary haemodialysis for days 5, 6, 8, and 9. 

The patient was diagnosed with functional (paralytic) ileus after suffering from vomit-like bile. The patient was treated conservatively, with discontinuation of solid food intake and total parenteral nutrition (TPN) management. A nasointestinal tube was inserted to keep the intestinal tract at rest.

The patient's urine output increased, and the patient began a liquid diet. Liver function improved gradually, and the man was discharged on day 38 after confirmation that there was no relapse of abdominal symptoms.

Discharge Medications:

The patient was given oral prednisolone and tazobactam− piperacillin and levofloxacin.

Follow-Up:

The patient was advised to follow up with their primary care physician for continued management of their condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was for SARS-CoV-2 infection (COVID-19), confirmed by PCR, which caused the respiratory and renal failure, fever and diarrhoea. COVID-19 is classified under the special-purpose chapter U, category U07 (U07.1, COVID-19 virus identified). The ileus, dialysis and other complications were secondary to it.

CODE: U07
